Render a document to a file

Source: R/render.R
pub_render.Rd

Writes a document (see pub_doc()) as a report file and returns its path. The report spec (see pub_report_spec()) sets the details, such as the templates, front matter, table of contents, page, figure settings and post-processors.

Usage

pub_render(
  doc,
  format = c("html", "docx", "pdf", "md"),
  file = NULL,
  spec = pub_report_spec(format),
  meta = list(),
  cache = NULL,
  pdf_engine = c("xelatex", "typst"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

doc

A pub_doc.

format

Output format: "html", "docx", "pdf" or "md".

file

Path of the output file; default (NULL): pub_output_filename() in the session's temporary directory.

spec

A pub_report_spec() for format. The default, pub_report_spec(format), gives what is described in Details.

meta

Named list of render-time metadata (see Details and pub_doc()), e.g. list(author = session$user, app = "myapp", version = "1.2.0").

cache

A pub_cache() or NULL (render every figure). Figures are cached as in pub_html().

pdf_engine

Engine of PDF files: "xelatex" or "typst".

quiet

FALSE: pandoc's warnings (e.g. about missing fonts or images) become R warnings.

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

Formats

formatResultNeeds
"html"a standalone pagenothing
"docx"a Word documentpandoc (>= 3.6)
"pdf"a PDFpandoc and xelatex or Typst
"md"a Markdown filenothing

HTML

  • The page is self-contained: stylesheet, images and the scripts and stylesheets of widgets are inlined.

  • Math (MathJax) is loaded from a CDN, so it needs an internet connection.

  • Files that widgets load by relative URLs (fonts, images or data referenced in their stylesheets, attachments) are not included, so such widgets may miss them.

DOCX (via pub_markdown() and pandoc)

  • A4 with numbered headings, tables as native Word tables, math as Word equations, figures as PNG images (200 dpi) and landscape sections for items that need them.

  • Tables of contents and caption numbers are Word fields: Word updates them when you agree to it as the file is opened.

  • With lock = TRUE in the spec, the header, the footer and the tables and figures are locked against accidental editing and deletion (single tables and figures opt out with pub_set_meta(locked = FALSE)). By default (lock = NULL), only tables and figures with pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE) are locked; lock = FALSE locks nothing. See pub_pp_docx_header_footer() and pub_pp_docx_lock(), which run automatically before the spec's own post-processors unless the spec lists them.

PDF (via pub_markdown() and pandoc) with the pdf_engine:

  • "xelatex" (default): needs a TeX distribution such as TinyTeX with the LaTeX packages that huxtable needs (see huxtable::install_latex_dependencies()) plus pdflscape, fancyhdr, lastpage, float and newunicodechar.

  • "typst": needs Typst (see "Finding Typst" below).

With either engine, the PDF has A4 pages, figures as PNG images (200 dpi; the spec's figure argument allows vector images) and tables that break across pages and repeat their header rows. Table cells, table captions, headers and footers show as typed, while other text gets the typography of LaTeX or Typst (e.g. in LaTeX " becomes a curly quote).

Markdown

A Markdown file (see pub_markdown()) that needs no pandoc. Its figures go to the directory <name>_files next to it (files of the same name there are overwritten).

Header and footer lines

DOCX and PDF files show the header and footer lines of the document (see pub_doc()):

  • {trace} in a line is replaced by a line that says who rendered the report and when, e.g. "Jane Doe at 07-Oct-2026 12:00:00 UTC (myapp v1.2.0)" (see pub_trace_stamp()).

  • The footer gets "Page x / N" at the right unless the footer has a right part.

Title block and table of contents

The title block appears only if the document has a title, subtitle or author. A table of contents follows it if the document has sections, unless the document places one itself.

Render-time metadata

meta holds information about the act of rendering, e.g. the author of the current session, the application and its version:

  • It is merged over the document's own metadata: its entries win and NULL removes an entry.

  • time is the render time unless one of them has a time.

  • File name, title block, {trace}, front matter and post-processors all see the merged result.

Passing this here instead of to the pipeline keeps the layout step from becoming outdated with every render.

Error items

With on_error = "continue", a failed step doesn't stop the pipeline. A layout step then receives the failure and may place it in the document as an error item (see pub_doc()). By default, pub_render() refuses such a document, so that a report never contains errors. For a final report, therefore, run the pipeline with the default on_error = "stop".

For drafts, you can instead run the pipeline with on_error = "continue" and set pub_report_spec(error_items = "show"). The document is then rendered, with the error items shown as error boxes and a warning.

Good to know

  • Rendering needs neither the pipeline nor a Shiny session.

  • Every call works in a fresh temporary directory. The file is only written if everything (including post-processors) succeeded.

Finding Typst

Typst is taken from the environment variable PUBFLOW_TYPST (the typst executable or its directory), else from the PATH, else from Quarto's installation (found by QUARTO_PATH or on the PATH).

See also

pub_report_spec(), pub_trace_stamp(), pub_html(), pub_markdown(), pub_output_filename()

Examples

doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section("Results", pub_text("All batches meet the limits.")),
    title = "Demo report"
)
noon <- as.POSIXct("2026-10-05 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
path <- pub_render(doc, file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"),
                   meta = list(author = "Jane Doe", time = noon))
file.exists(path)
#> [1] TRUE
basename(pub_output_filename(list(title = "Demo report", time = noon),
                             "html"))
#> [1] "20261005T120000Z_demo_report.html"
